reuse.why: getDateWithSkippedWeekend is extended and reused, but the server's getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange write their own daily-skip check and weekend-or-holiday test (config.holidays?.includes(dayFromDate(...))) instead of using the shared isWeekendOrHoliday/filterDailyNonHolidays, so they miss the MM-DD rule.

duplication.why: The 'daily: skip weekend/holiday, otherwise move' decision is written three times (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates as a flatMap, getDatesInRange as a for-loop), the non-working-day predicate exists in two versions, and schedule-template gets its own skip-weekend ternary helper.

placement.why: The core rule sits in shared/schedules.ts where it belongs, but the per-occurrence adjustment used by the new range handler and upcoming dates is re-built in server/schedules/app.ts rather than living next to it.

scope.why: All edits serve the four steps; the schedule-template helper extraction and the rule-utils holidays pass-through are related.

maintainability.why: Holiday matching already diverges between copies (server copies only match full dates), and the over-fetch heuristics (holidays.length + 7, +2) are repeated ad hoc; each future rule change must be made in several places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange test d.isWeekend(date) || config.holidays?.includes(dayFromDate(date)) themselves instead of the shared isWeekendOrHoliday/filterDailyNonHolidays in shared/schedules.ts.

disguised_duplication.where: The same skip-daily/move-others per-occurrence logic is reshaped as a flatMap in getUpcomingDates, a for-loop in getDatesInRange and a filter+guard in getNextDate; the predicate is re-spelled as includes(dayFromDate) vs isWeekendOrHoliday.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a skipDailyWeekends special case (filter branch and the !skipDailyWeekends guard on the move); getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange re-implement the daily/holiday decision instead of calling the shared helpers.
